newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi protests to Zaire over attack in Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Burundi protests to Zaire over attack in Kinshasa.

text.p: Burundi has protested strongly to Zaire after its ambassador's residence in Kinshasa was looted by troops and students at the weekend, state-run Radio Burundi said on Monday.
"The government of Burundi protests indignantly to the Zairean government and demands it ensures the safety of all Burundians living in Zaire," said a foreign ministry statement quoted by the radio.
Burundian diplomats and embassy staff were threatened when the ambassador's residence was looted on Saturday, said the statement, which took Burundi's relations with Zaire to a new low.

Burundi has repeatedly denied accusations by Zaire that its Tutsi-dominated army invaded eastern Zaire and is fighting alongside ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels who control the east Zairean town of Uvira and much of Zaire's border with Burundi.
Zaire argues the armies of Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda are supporting the rebels to create a pro-Tutsi security zone along their western borders, a charge which all three countries deny.
Diplomats in the Burundian capital however say the Tutsi rebels in Zaire are cooperating with Burundi's army in screening thousands of Burundian male Hutu refugees attempting to return home.
Up to 140 men have disappeared in the last two weeks and were suspected killed by Burundian troops in no man's land between the two countries after screening, diplomats and aid workers say.

Burundian authorities however deny Burundian troops are killing returning refugees. Hutu Burundian rebels fighting the Burundian army were based in refugee camps in eastern Zaire before the Tutsi Zairean rebels seized the town of Uvira.
Around 10,000 Burundian Hutu refugees have returned to a transit site at Gatumba in Burundi since last Saturday from refugee camps after being told to go home by the Banyamulenge rebels.
